article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Evening Brief
article.dek: The Value card is back, both starting quarterbacks got their final answer, and the Detroit line moved again.

items.headline: The Value card is back, and it is a coin flip
paragraphs: The Value card has a pick tonight: the New York Giants +6 at -110 on DraftKings against Jacksonville, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET. It was empty this morning.
Be clear about what this one is. The app gives the Giants about a 50% chance to cover the six points. The edge is a hair above zero. That is the thinnest kind of Value card, a nudge, not a statement.
The other two cards did not move. Hit Rate is still the Jaguars moneyline at -255 on FanDuel. Balanced is still the Jets +3 at -105 on DraftKings.
items.takeaway: Value is back with Giants +6 at -110, the thinnest kind of edge. Hit Rate is Jaguars moneyline -255, Balanced is Jets +3 at -105, both unchanged.

sources.label: NFL EDGE app

items.headline: Both starting quarterbacks got their final answer
paragraphs: Geno Smith is cleared. He practiced fully on Friday, carries no injury designation, and will start for the Jets at the Chargers on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET. The app lists him as the Jets' expected starter.

Baker Mayfield is questionable, but the news points the same way it did this morning. He was limited again on Friday with the foot and right thumb injuries, and head coach Todd Bowles said he is trending in the right direction to play. The app lists Mayfield, not Jalon Daniels, as Tampa Bay's expected starter for Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET in Detroit.
Questionable is not cleared. The final word on Mayfield comes with the inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Geno Smith is cleared and will start Sunday. Mayfield is questionable but expected to start; the inactives settle it.

items.headline: Arizona is likely on its fourth quarterback in four weeks
paragraphs: Carson Beck is questionable with back spasms. He did not practice on Friday, and head coach Mike LaFleur said the Cardinals will proceed as if Josh Johnson starts on Sunday at Kansas City.

One thing to know: the app has not caught up yet. It still lists Beck as Arizona's expected starter. If your book's Kansas City line moved on the Johnson news, do not trust the app's old number. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app run it back through the model on the real price.
items.takeaway: Beck is questionable and unlikely to start; Josh Johnson is the likely starter. The app still lists Beck, so Check your price.

items.headline: The rest of the final injury report
paragraphs: Tampa Bay ruled out safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Josh Hayes (knee). Detroit ruled out center Cade Mays (ankle) and has six players questionable, including three cornerbacks.

The Jets ruled out wide receivers Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs). Kansas City running back Kenneth Walker III is out against Arizona. Minnesota is without wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) and quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) for Sunday night in Mexico City.
Buffalo tight end Dalton Kincaid is doubtful against Miami. Las Vegas tight end Brock Bowers and Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey are questionable.
items.takeaway: Winfield Jr., Hayes, Mays, Walker III, Addison and Murray are out. Kincaid is doubtful; Bowers and McConkey are questionable.

items.headline: Weather: rain in three spots, wind in Chicago and Kansas City
paragraphs: Chicago is still the wettest and windiest spot. Saints at Bears, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET: rain likely, about 57 degrees, wind about 15 mph from the west.

Philadelphia has rain too. Steelers at Eagles, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET: rain, about 62 degrees, wind about 5 mph, a 76% chance of precipitation at kickoff. At MetLife, Jaguars at Giants, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET: light rain likely, about 60 degrees, wind about 7 mph.

Kansas City is cold and breezy but dry: about 48 degrees, wind about 15 mph from the north, gusts to 24. Buffalo is mild at about 64 degrees. Denver is sunny and about 45 degrees. Sunday night in Mexico City is about 66 degrees and mainly clear. Detroit and the Chargers play indoors, and the Dallas roof is expected closed.
Weather is a fact, not an edge. The app prices the games, not the forecast.
items.takeaway: Rain likely in Chicago, Philadelphia and at MetLife. Wind about 15 mph in Chicago and Kansas City. Mild everywhere else.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: How to read tonight's three cards
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. It forgoes value for win probability. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. A likely winner is not the same thing as a good price.

Jaguars moneyline -255 on FanDuel. At -255, every $2.55 you risk wins $1. The app gives Jacksonville about a 76% chance; the market says about 70%. The app's play-through is -264. That is the price where it stops being a bet, and -255 still clears it. It is the app's biggest stake of the week at 1.25 units.
Balanced is Jets +3 at -105 on DraftKings. The app calls it about a coin flip to cover, and the play-through is -108. Close to even money, a good starting point if you are new to this.
Value is Giants +6 at -110. Value is always the app's +EV play. This one is barely +EV, so treat it as what it is: the app found a price a hair better than its number, not a strong opinion.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate is Jaguars moneyline -255, the most likely winner. Balanced is Jets +3 at -105, about a coin flip. Value is Giants +6 at -110, barely over the line.

sources.label: NFL EDGE app

items.headline: The app still thinks the big spreads are too fat, and it still bet none of them
paragraphs: The model's margins against the DraftKings spreads: Chiefs by about 6.3 against a 16.5-point spread. Bills by about 3.4 against 16.5. Bears by about 0.2 against 11.5. Lions by about 1.7 against 5.5. Steelers by about 1.8 against 3.5. Bengals by about 5.2 against 6.0.
The closest one is the Jaguars game. The app has Jacksonville by about 5.7 against a 6-point spread, and that is where the Value card came from, on the other side at +6.

None of the big underdogs cleared the bar for a card. A gap is the start of the work, not the bet. If your book has a better number than the app's, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app run it back through the model and give you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Six big spreads, six big model gaps, zero cards on the dogs. The gap alone is not the bet. Check your price.

items.headline: The tickets still love Detroit. The money is still heavier on Tampa Bay.
paragraphs: DraftKings' own published figures for Tampa Bay at Detroit, read this evening: 88% of the bets are on the Lions, but only 71% of the money is. Tampa Bay has 12% of the bets and 29% of the money.
That is the same split the morning brief showed, and it still says the same thing. The crowd is on the favorite. The bigger bets are on the dog.
A split like this is decision context, not a pick. It does not override the app, and it does not tell you to fade the public. It tells you where the price might go next.
items.takeaway: Most tickets are on Detroit, most money is not. Tampa Bay has 12% of the bets but 29% of the money, the same split as this morning.

items.headline: What moved since the morning, and what to watch
paragraphs: The line kept moving toward Tampa Bay. Detroit was -6.0 on DraftKings this morning. It is -5.5 now, and -4.5 on FanDuel. The split is still there, but the cheap Tampa Bay price the morning flagged is partly gone. Waiting cost a half-point today.

Watch the Detroit number from here. If it drifts back toward -6 or -6.5 with no new bad Bucs news, Tampa Bay gets cheaper again, and that is the same football opinion for a better price. If it keeps moving toward Tampa Bay, the wait is over.
One thing kills the wait: Mayfield. He is questionable, and the inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff. If he is ruled out, the whole read changes, so check the final designations first.
items.takeaway: Detroit moved from -6.0 to -5.5 on DraftKings, so the cheap Tampa Bay price is partly gone. Watch for a drift back toward -6, and check Mayfield's status first.

items.headline: The Value card appeared, and Detroit moved again
paragraphs: The Value card is new since this morning: Giants +6 at -110 on DraftKings. Nothing else on the cards changed. Hit Rate is still Jaguars moneyline -255 on FanDuel, and Balanced is still Jets +3 at -105 on DraftKings.

Detroit moved again. The Lions were -6.0 on DraftKings this morning and are -5.5 now, -4.5 on FanDuel. Pittsburgh moved too: the Steelers are -3.5 on DraftKings, a point shorter than the 4.5 the board showed Thursday evening. FanDuel still has Pittsburgh -4.5.

Everything else held still: Kansas City -16.5, Buffalo -16.5, Chicago -11.5, Cincinnati -6.0 on DraftKings, Jacksonville -6.0 on DraftKings, and the Jets +3. The board refreshes every morning and evening, so check back tomorrow morning for the next read.
items.takeaway: Value appeared with Giants +6 at -110. Detroit moved to -5.5 on DraftKings, Pittsburgh to -3.5. Everything else held.

items.headline: Final designations are in, so check your prices now
paragraphs: Both quarterback answers are in, and the final designations are out. Check your Tampa Bay and Jets prices now. If Check says bet on a good number, bet now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number on Sunday, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too, and the Sunday late rush on big-name teams can push a line past the app's playable number.
The one thing still open is Mayfield. The inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff, and that is when his status is truly settled.
One more thing, and it matters every week: settlement is manual. There is no auto-settle. The tracker only works if you are honest with yourself, so log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Check your Tampa Bay and Jets prices now, and bet now if Check says so. Log the losers too, the tracker only works if you are honest.
